style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Technical Services, Planning Sections monitors AD/SBs and other documents from manufacturers related to CAT II/III operation and accordingly modifies CAT II/III maintenance program. Technical Services, Planning Sections also needs to timely update CAT II/III maintenance procedure and inform these modifications to Flight Operations Department, Supply Section, Technical Quality Assurance Department, Flight Ops Department and contracted maintenance organizations.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.7.4	Controlling equipment related to CAT II/III:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">All equipment replacements need to comply with IPC. Equipment is not allowed to be installed on aircraft if they are not listed in IPC.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.8	Maintenance program</strong></p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.8.1	Scheduled Maintenance</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	All maintenance tasks required for CAT II/III shall be covered in Aircraft Maintenance Program (AMP). Those tasks must be performed even low visibility systems are not used.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Before each flight and after a maintenance check, certifying staff shall check whether the aircraft is eligible for CAT II/III operation.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.8.2	Unscheduled maintenance</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">For unscheduled maintenance, this CAT II/III maintenance schedule shall define:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	Trouble shooting, Equipment Repair and Adjustment related to CAT II/III (refer to 2.25.9- Procedure).</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	CAT II/III upgrade/downgrade procedure (refer to 2.25.9-Procedure).</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9	Procedures</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">In addition to normal aircraft maintenance requirements, the following criteria must be met to maintain CAT II/III capability for an aircraft. AMM tests required for CAT II/III operation must be done during trouble shooting, equipment repair and adjustment.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">For an aircraft deferred defect related to CAT II/III, one ADD shall be raised and CAT II/III capability will be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I according to MEL.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.1	Trouble Shooting, Equipment Repair and Adjustment</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">After a repair or an adjustment is performed on the equipment, the CAT II/III revalidation of this equipment must be performed by the corresponding AMM test:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	For Airbus aircrafts, perform:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	All related testing tasks which are required in AMM; and</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	For CAT II/III, perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.2	After the maintenance check</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	All repairs and adjustments performed during maintenance check must comply with 2.25.8.1.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Aircraft CAT II/III status will be checked and processed during the next pre-flight check (refer to 2.25.8.3. and 2.25.8.9.)</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.3	CAT II/III Downgrading</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Important Note:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	CAT III can be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">The aircraft autoland operational status shall be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I, under any of the following conditions:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	Engineering modification regarding AD/SB that affects to CAT II/III performance.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Following the occurrence of a defect to any one or more of the aircraft systems which are essential to CAT II/III operations.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	When the integrity of at least one of the systems essential to CAT II/III operations is in doubt.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">d)	When the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">e)	Failure to complete the functional tests of CAT II//III required equipment.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.4	Downgrading due to technical issues:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">If an AD/SB requires downgrading CAT II/III status, Technical Services Section will process downgrading CAT II/III to CAT I or CAT II accordingly.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.5	Downgrading due to Autoland Status reported unsuccessful with the relevant aircraft defect:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Certifying staff shall check Autoland Monitoring form placed on cockpit. If the last autoland is unsuccessful, and the relevant aircraft defect found and recorded in the TechLog, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I in accordance to the procedure of Downgrading due to Deferred Defects (refer to 2.25.9.7).</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.6	Downgrading due to Chronic (or Repetitive) Discrepancies:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">MOC shall handle monitoring and detecting of a chronic (or repetitive) CAT II/III equipment/system malfunction. An aircraft experiencing chronic (or repetitive) discrepancy shall be downgraded to CAT I status in accordance with the procedure of Downgrading due to Deferred Defects (refer to 2.25.9.7).</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.7	Downgrading due to Deferred Defects:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">When the landing capability of the aircraft is impacted by an inoperative item in according with MEL, certifying staff shall:</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.7.1	Applicable for ETLB</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	A defect shall be recorded in ETLB Open item list. New defect shall be created when certifying staff enters “New Work Order” data on ETLB with maintenance mode</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Enter the data in the description text in ETLB defect entry with the statement: “NON CAT II AND III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION”</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	 Certifying staff shall defer Workorder and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT II AND III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” and then A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">d)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">e)	Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item shall be recorded in ETLB Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item list.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">f)	Contracted maintenance organization shall inform to MOC about aircraft CAT II/III downgraded immediately by using ADD Notice and other means of communication.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.7.2	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	Raise an ADD as a normal procedure and include certification statement “NON CAT II and III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” in Technical Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Write a note of “NON CAT II/III OPERATION” in “Notice to Crews” form QDF 104V to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	Make entry in ADD log as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT II and III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” in the ADD Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Contracted maintenance organization shall inform to MOC about aircraft CAT II/III downgraded immediately by using ADD Notice and other means of communication.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.8	Downgrading due to the aircraft NOT performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">During the daily/stayover check or equivalent check, certifying staff shall check the AUTOLAND status in ETLB (or the Autoland form).</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.8.1	Applicable for ETLB</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	If the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days and if there is no similar ADD raised previously, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT I as follows:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	A non-airworthiness defect shall be recorded in ETLB Open item list. New defect shall be created when:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	PIC enters “New Complaint” data on ETLB with Cockpit mode</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	or Certifying staff enters “New Work Order” data on ETLB with maintenance mode</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	Certifying staff shall defer Workorder and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I (Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations). The due date of this ADD is 30 days.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Enter data in the Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED”</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">4)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">5)	Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item shall be recorded in ETLB Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item list.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">6)	Upon notification of the aircraft's CAT II/III upgraded status, MOC will inform OMC about this status to coordinate operation.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.8.2	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	If the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days and if there is no similar ADD raised previously, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT I as follows:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Raise a non-airworthiness ADD as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in Technical Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I. The due date of this ADD is 30 days.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	Write a note of “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in “Notice to Crews” form QDF 104V to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Make entry in ADD log as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in the ADD Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I. Contracted maintenance organization shall inform MOC then MOC notify to relevant Departments such as OMC, Flight Ops and the next destination airport by telephone, FAX or email (or equivalent) about aircraft CAT II downgraded to coordinate operation</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.9	CAT II/III Upgrading</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Important Note:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	CAT I can be upgraded to CAT II or CAT III</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	If the aircraft has been downgraded due to defect, aircraft shall only be upgraded to CAT II/III operation if:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">i)	Applicable for ETLB</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Defects related to CAT II/III are rectified by appropriate certifying staff in accordance with AMM requirements; and</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	Certifying staff holding category B2 only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Certifying staff shall choose “Add action” or “Add action to Last Work Step” button and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “A/C RETURNED TO CAT II” or “A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” in accordance with MME 2.1.2 and then make “Close Work order” for this item.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">4)	Certifying staff shall close workorder and then Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation is cleared;</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">5)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">ii)	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Defects related to CAT II/III are rectified by appropriate certifying staff in accordance with AMM requirements; and</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	Certifying staff holding category B2 only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">NOTE: certifying staff in possession of a category other than B2 authorization may rectify defects related to system not affecting the function of the auto-pilot (e.g. wipers, rain repellent or window heat) to upgrade CAT I to CAT II as appropriate without performing Land Cat III Capability test. Refer table 2 for such equipment. Upon defect rectification, the statement “A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” shall be recorded in Tech log.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	If the aircraft has been downgraded to CAT I due to NO performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days. Aircraft shall only be upgraded to CAT III operation if:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">i)	Applicable for ETLB</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Certifying staff holding category B2 shall only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM; or</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	A performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Upon performance of LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST, certifying staff B2 must choose “Add action” or “Add action to Last Work Step” button and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with adding certificate statement in accordance with MME 2.1.2 as follows:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">“LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST CARRIED OUT-SATIS. A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” or</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">4)	Certifying staff shall close workorder and then Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation is cleared;</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">5)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">ii)	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Certifying staff holding category B2 shall only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM; or</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	A performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	Upon performance of LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST, the certifying staff holding B2 must include the certificate statement:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">“LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST CARRIED OUT-SATIS. A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” as appropriate in Tech log. The AMM task reference number for the Land CAT III capability test must be recorded.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">d)	NTC and ADD shall be cleared. Certifying staff/ Contracted AMO/ VJC PCC should also advise MOC on the upgraded status of the aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">e)	Upon notification of the aircraft’s CAT II/III upgraded status, MOC will inform OMC about this status to coordinate operation.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.9.10	Requirements for certifying staff:</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	All certifying staff shall to be trained CAT II/III maintenance procedures.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Only certifying staff possession of the B2 category authorization may upgrade an aircraft from CAT I to CAT II/III when serviceability is proven, by a successful Land CAT III Capability Test IAW applicable AMM.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.10	CAT II/III Status Control</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	MOC and OMC shall control the CAT II/III status by ADD related to CAT II/III downgraded or upgraded.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	CAT II/III status is noted to ETLB Downgrades/Limitations item list and ETLB Open item list.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	Contracted maintenance organization shall inform MOC about the CAT II/III status.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.25.11	Minimum Equipment List</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	MMEL is the Airbus dispatch document, which constitutes a reference for VJC to create its own MEL used in operations.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Flight Operations Engineering Department shall set up VJC MEL based on the MMEL and CAAV requirements. 2.25.1	Background
Although CAT II/III represents a significant investment for an airline, it is the most effective way in which an airline can maintain its schedule throughout the year without any diversions due to the bad weather. This results in lower costs incurred by otherwise expensive diversions and passenger compensation, as well as preventing degradation of the airline's image.
2.25.2	Purpose
This procedure helps VJC follow the regulations set by CAAV in order to certify that its aircrafts are eligible for CAT II/III operation. This ensures that the aircraft can land in low visibility condition with a safety level as in normal conditions.
2.25.3	Scope of application
This maintenance procedure is applied for A320/A321/A330 VJC fleet.
2.25.4	Aircraft Effectivity
Refer to the VJC Operation specification approved by CAAV for the CAT II/III authorization and the list of VJC aircraft authorized for CAT II/III operations.

d)	AIRBUS Getting Grips to CAT II / CAT III operation

2.25.6	Responsibility
a)	Engineering Director is responsible for compliance with all requirements of the CAT II/III maintenance program.
b)	Technical Training Manager shall be responsible for:
1)	Establishing the training syllabus that meets CAAV requirements relating to CAT II/III maintenance;
2)	Giving CAT III maintenance training to the contracted AMO, contracted involved Partner and involved staff within VJC.
c)	TQA Manager is responsible for:
1)	Ensuring the compliance with CAT II/III requirements set in this MME and the relevant VAR;
2)	Approval for training syllabus and instructors
d)	Reliability Manager is responsible for developing the reliability program that is covered the CAT II/III maintenance program to monitor, track and control the CAT II/III operation status of the VJC aircraft;
e)	Technical Services, Planning Managers are responsible for:
1)	Creating the CAT II/III Maintenance procedures necessary to ensure continued airworthiness relative to low visibility operations;
2)	Contacting the manufacturer if necessary;
3)	Evaluating the modification related to CAT II/III operation;
4)	Monitoring technical alerts from reliability program;
5)	Setting up and distributing CAT II/III maintenance documents;
6)	Providing technical documents updates.
f)	Contracted Maintenance Organization (AMO) is responsible for compliance with the maintenance procedures set in MME.
g)	FOE Manager is responsible for:
1)	Setting up, modifying and controlling MEL;
2)	By working with flight crew, Flight Operations Department is responsible for making sure auto landing performed with satisfactory low visibility system operational use;
3)	Informing Engineering and Maintenance Department about AFM, MEL document update.
2.25.7	Configuration of VJC A320/A321/A330 Fleet
2.25.7.1	The curent configuration of VJC operated A320/A321/A330
On all Airbus A320/A321/A330 aircraft CAT II/III are inherent functions of the basic design standard of the aircraft. Therefore, related tasks are covered by the respective maintenance program (by ATA chapter) in MPD that VJC AMP is strictly followed. However, VJC should comply with the supplemental CAAV requirements when applicable.
2.25.7.2	Configuration Monitoring and Modification
a)	All aircraft equipment and systems related to CAT II/III operation must be fully described in MEL (and CDL, DDG if applicable) documents. When there’s a defect detected by aircraft systems or flight crew report relevant to CAT II/III operation, certifying staffs have to use MEL documents for dispatching the aircraft.
b)	Flight crews should engage autopilot and auto-throttle in every flight to increase CAT II/III operation reliability.
c)	The following configuration requirements in Table 2 for A320/A321 and Table 3 for A330 are for maintenance control and reliability program reference only, not for dispatching the aircrafts.

2.25.7.3	Technical Bulletin and Airworthiness Directive
Technical Services, Planning Sections monitors AD/SBs and other documents from manufacturers related to CAT II/III operation and accordingly modifies CAT II/III maintenance program. Technical Services, Planning Sections also needs to timely update CAT II/III maintenance procedure and inform these modifications to Flight Operations Department, Supply Section, Technical Quality Assurance Department, Flight Ops Department and contracted maintenance organizations.
2.25.7.4	Controlling equipment related to CAT II/III:
All equipment replacements need to comply with IPC. Equipment is not allowed to be installed on aircraft if they are not listed in IPC.
2.25.8	Maintenance program
2.25.8.1	Scheduled Maintenance
a)	All maintenance tasks required for CAT II/III shall be covered in Aircraft Maintenance Program (AMP). Those tasks must be performed even low visibility systems are not used.
b)	Before each flight and after a maintenance check, certifying staff shall check whether the aircraft is eligible for CAT II/III operation.
2.25.8.2	Unscheduled maintenance
For unscheduled maintenance, this CAT II/III maintenance schedule shall define:
a)	Trouble shooting, Equipment Repair and Adjustment related to CAT II/III (refer to 2.25.9- Procedure).
b)	CAT II/III upgrade/downgrade procedure (refer to 2.25.9-Procedure).
2.25.9	Procedures
In addition to normal aircraft maintenance requirements, the following criteria must be met to maintain CAT II/III capability for an aircraft. AMM tests required for CAT II/III operation must be done during trouble shooting, equipment repair and adjustment.
For an aircraft deferred defect related to CAT II/III, one ADD shall be raised and CAT II/III capability will be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I according to MEL.
2.25.9.1	Trouble Shooting, Equipment Repair and Adjustment
After a repair or an adjustment is performed on the equipment, the CAT II/III revalidation of this equipment must be performed by the corresponding AMM test:
a)	For Airbus aircrafts, perform:
1)	All related testing tasks which are required in AMM; and
2)	For CAT II/III, perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST.
2.25.9.2	After the maintenance check
a)	All repairs and adjustments performed during maintenance check must comply with 2.25.8.1.
b)	Aircraft CAT II/III status will be checked and processed during the next pre-flight check (refer to 2.25.8.3. and 2.25.8.9.)
2.25.9.3	CAT II/III Downgrading
Important Note:
	CAT III can be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I.
The aircraft autoland operational status shall be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I, under any of the following conditions:
a)	Engineering modification regarding AD/SB that affects to CAT II/III performance.
b)	Following the occurrence of a defect to any one or more of the aircraft systems which are essential to CAT II/III operations.
c)	When the integrity of at least one of the systems essential to CAT II/III operations is in doubt.
d)	When the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days.
e)	Failure to complete the functional tests of CAT II//III required equipment.
2.25.9.4	Downgrading due to technical issues:
If an AD/SB requires downgrading CAT II/III status, Technical Services Section will process downgrading CAT II/III to CAT I or CAT II accordingly.
2.25.9.5	Downgrading due to Autoland Status reported unsuccessful with the relevant aircraft defect:
Certifying staff shall check Autoland Monitoring form placed on cockpit. If the last autoland is unsuccessful, and the relevant aircraft defect found and recorded in the TechLog, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT II or CAT I in accordance to the procedure of Downgrading due to Deferred Defects (refer to 2.25.9.7).
2.25.9.6	Downgrading due to Chronic (or Repetitive) Discrepancies:
MOC shall handle monitoring and detecting of a chronic (or repetitive) CAT II/III equipment/system malfunction. An aircraft experiencing chronic (or repetitive) discrepancy shall be downgraded to CAT I status in accordance with the procedure of Downgrading due to Deferred Defects (refer to 2.25.9.7).
2.25.9.7	Downgrading due to Deferred Defects:
When the landing capability of the aircraft is impacted by an inoperative item in according with MEL, certifying staff shall:
2.25.9.7.1	Applicable for ETLB
a)	A defect shall be recorded in ETLB Open item list. New defect shall be created when certifying staff enters “New Work Order” data on ETLB with maintenance mode
b)	Enter the data in the description text in ETLB defect entry with the statement: “NON CAT II AND III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION”
c)	 Certifying staff shall defer Workorder and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT II AND III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” and then A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.
d)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.
e)	Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item shall be recorded in ETLB Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item list.
f)	Contracted maintenance organization shall inform to MOC about aircraft CAT II/III downgraded immediately by using ADD Notice and other means of communication.
2.25.9.7.2	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log
a)	Raise an ADD as a normal procedure and include certification statement “NON CAT II and III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” in Technical Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.
b)	Write a note of “NON CAT II/III OPERATION” in “Notice to Crews” form QDF 104V to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.
c)	Make entry in ADD log as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT II and III OPERATION” or “NON CAT III OPERATION” in the ADD Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I or CAT II as appropriate.
Contracted maintenance organization shall inform to MOC about aircraft CAT II/III downgraded immediately by using ADD Notice and other means of communication.
2.25.9.8	Downgrading due to the aircraft NOT performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach:
During the daily/stayover check or equivalent check, certifying staff shall check the AUTOLAND status in ETLB (or the Autoland form).
2.25.9.8.1	Applicable for ETLB
a)	If the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days and if there is no similar ADD raised previously, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT I as follows:
1)	A non-airworthiness defect shall be recorded in ETLB Open item list. New defect shall be created when:
	PIC enters “New Complaint” data on ETLB with Cockpit mode
	or Certifying staff enters “New Work Order” data on ETLB with maintenance mode
2)	Certifying staff shall defer Workorder and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I (Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations). The due date of this ADD is 30 days.
3)	Enter data in the Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED”
4)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.
5)	Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item shall be recorded in ETLB Aircraft Downgrades/Limitations item list.
6)	Upon notification of the aircraft's CAT II/III upgraded status, MOC will inform OMC about this status to coordinate operation.
2.25.9.8.2	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log
a)	If the aircraft has not performed a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days and if there is no similar ADD raised previously, the affected aircraft shall be downgraded to CAT I as follows:
1)	Raise a non-airworthiness ADD as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in Technical Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I. The due date of this ADD is 30 days.
2)	Write a note of “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in “Notice to Crews” form QDF 104V to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I.
3)	Make entry in ADD log as a normal procedure and add the statement “NON CAT III OPERATION DUE TO AUTOLAND NOT PERFORMED” in the ADD Log to indicate that A/C is downgraded to CAT I. Contracted maintenance organization shall inform MOC then MOC notify to relevant Departments such as OMC, Flight Ops and the next destination airport by telephone, FAX or email (or equivalent) about aircraft CAT II downgraded to coordinate operation
2.25.9.9	CAT II/III Upgrading
Important Note:
	CAT I can be upgraded to CAT II or CAT III
a)	If the aircraft has been downgraded due to defect, aircraft shall only be upgraded to CAT II/III operation if:
i)	Applicable for ETLB
1)	Defects related to CAT II/III are rectified by appropriate certifying staff in accordance with AMM requirements; and
2)	Certifying staff holding category B2 only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM.
3)	Certifying staff shall choose “Add action” or “Add action to Last Work Step” button and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with the statement: “A/C RETURNED TO CAT II” or “A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” in accordance with MME 2.1.2 and then make “Close Work order” for this item.
4)	Certifying staff shall close workorder and then Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation is cleared;
5)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.
ii)	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log
1)	Defects related to CAT II/III are rectified by appropriate certifying staff in accordance with AMM requirements; and
2)	Certifying staff holding category B2 only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM.
NOTE: certifying staff in possession of a category other than B2 authorization may rectify defects related to system not affecting the function of the auto-pilot (e.g. wipers, rain repellent or window heat) to upgrade CAT I to CAT II as appropriate without performing Land Cat III Capability test. Refer table 2 for such equipment. Upon defect rectification, the statement “A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” shall be recorded in Tech log.
b)	If the aircraft has been downgraded to CAT I due to NO performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III approach during the previous 30 days. Aircraft shall only be upgraded to CAT III operation if:
i)	Applicable for ETLB
1)	Certifying staff holding category B2 shall only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM; or
2)	A performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III.
3)	Upon performance of LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST, certifying staff B2 must choose “Add action” or “Add action to Last Work Step” button and enter the data in the action text in ETLB workorder detail with adding certificate statement in accordance with MME 2.1.2 as follows:
“LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST CARRIED OUT-SATIS. A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” or
4)	Certifying staff shall close workorder and then Aircraft Downgrade/Limitation is cleared;
5)	Just after complete the ADD log, certifying staff shall synchronize data to Master device and certifying staff should also advise MOC on the new status of the aircraft.
ii)	Applicable for Paper-Based Aircraft Technical Log
1)	Certifying staff holding category B2 shall only perform LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST successfully as per applicable Airbus AMM; or
2)	A performance of a successful simulated or actual CAT III
c)	Upon performance of LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST, the certifying staff holding B2 must include the certificate statement:
“LAND CAT III CAPABILITY TEST CARRIED OUT-SATIS. A/C RETURNED TO CAT III” as appropriate in Tech log. The AMM task reference number for the Land CAT III capability test must be recorded.
d)	NTC and ADD shall be cleared. Certifying staff/ Contracted AMO/ VJC PCC should also advise MOC on the upgraded status of the aircraft.
e)	Upon notification of the aircraft’s CAT II/III upgraded status, MOC will inform OMC about this status to coordinate operation.
2.25.9.10	Requirements for certifying staff:
a)	All certifying staff shall to be trained CAT II/III maintenance procedures.
b)	Only certifying staff possession of the B2 category authorization may upgrade an aircraft from CAT I to CAT II/III when serviceability is proven, by a successful Land CAT III Capability Test IAW applicable AMM.
2.25.10	CAT II/III Status Control
a)	MOC and OMC shall control the CAT II/III status by ADD related to CAT II/III downgraded or upgraded.
b)	CAT II/III status is noted to ETLB Downgrades/Limitations item list and ETLB Open item list.
c)	Contracted maintenance organization shall inform MOC about the CAT II/III status.
2.25.11	Minimum Equipment List
a)	MMEL is the Airbus dispatch document, which constitutes a reference for VJC to create its own MEL used in operations.
b)	Flight Operations Engineering Department shall set up VJC MEL based on the MMEL and CAAV requirements. This MEL is included requirements for CAT II/III operation.
c)	The VJC MEL is the reference document to be used when checking the aircraft CAT II/III status following an equipment failure.
2.25.12	Training Program
a)	The VJC operator and contracted maintenance organizations have to conduct initial and recurrent trainings (according to VJC training policy) for maintenance or engineering staff who works directly or indirectly on aircraft such as TSE, maintenance planners, mechanics, certifying staff, MOC staff, maintenance inspectors, quality control staff, quality assurance staff, reliability staff, store inspectors and store controllers.
b)	Recurrent training shall be conducted annually or if a technical staff has not been involved in aircraft maintenance for an extended period of more than 6 months.
c)	The training material shall be reviewed and approved by Technical Training Manager, and the training syllabus shall be reviewed and approved by TQA Manager.
d)	Training program is described as follows:

2.25.13	Testing Equipment
a)	Contracted maintenance organizations shall ensure that all equipment/tools such as ILS test set related to CAT II/III are checked and repaired pursuant to CMM.
b)	All testing equipment shall be regularly calibrated pursuant to manufacturer documents with an interval not more than 12 months unless specifically defined by manufacturer documents.
c)	The Technical Quality Assurance Section audits the contracted maintenance organizations to ensure that VJC regulations are complied with.
2.25.14	Reliability Program and Quality Control
CAT II/III reliability program is a part of VJC reliability program.
	VJC will send the reliability program report to CAAV with the following contents:
a)	The number of CAT II/III landings.
b)	The number of successful CAT II/III landings per each aircraft type and Runway Visibility Reporting RVR (if applicable).
c)	The number of unsuccessful CAT II/III landings and the corresponding reasons.
d)	The number of unscheduled removals of equipment related to CAT II/III.
	Inputs for reliability program are from:
a)	Defects related to CAT II/III are collected from AMOS systems.
b)	ADD with respective CAT I/II operation database.
c)	Autoland monitoring form and monthly report form.
d)	Other reports from Pilot and certifying staffs.
The collected data shall be reviewed to assess reliability and safety concerns. Adverse trends shall be addressed promptly and aggressively to assure an acceptable level of reliability and high level of safety.
2.25.15	Records
The CAT II/III training records shall be recoded and filed by Technical Training Section.
2.25.16	Swapping/ Robbery of CAT II/III Component
In case of swapping/ robbery of CAT II/III Components or parts from other aircraft within the VJC fleet, the maintenance provider shall ensure that CAT II/III parts swapped or robbed from another aircraft currently have a CAT II/III Capable status so that the aircraft to be installed with this part retains its CAT II/III Capable status. If the part does not have this status, the receiving aircraft will be downgraded to CAT I. Details on swapping/ robbery of CAT II/III Component shall be referred to MME 1.6.7.

2.26.1	Purpose
This procedure describes the steps required to obtain a Special Flight Permit/ Ferry Flight Permit from the Civil Aviation Authority of Vietnam (CAAV) for an aircraft that is capable of safe flight but unable to meet applicable airworthiness requirements.
2.26.2	Scope of application
This procedure applies to all VietJet Air aircraft.
2.26.3	Reference
VAR 4.035, VAR 20 Subpart E, Appendix 1 to 20.075, VAR Part 12.035
2.26.4	Policy
It requires that aircraft types must conduct satisfactory demonstration flights during the CAAV certification process. This also applies to aircraft operating in designated special areas or using specialized navigation systems.
The CAAV may authorize deviations from this section if it finds that special circumstances make full compliance unnecessary.
2.26.5	Responsibilities
a)	Engineering department: Prepare the ferry flight dossier.
b)	SQA Director/TQA Manager: review and submit the ferry flight permit request to the CAAV and authority who had issued the ferry flight permit upon completion of the ferry flight.
c)	OMC, MOC: Coordinate with together to conduct the ferry flight.
2.26.6	Reference
VAR 4.035, VAR 20 Subpart E, Appendix 1 to 20.075
2.26.7	General
CAAV may issue Ferry Flight Permit to an aircraft that is capable of safe flight,but unable to meet applicable airworthiness requirements (e.g. COA expired or invalid due to scheduled maintenance tasks overdue, aircraft involved defect and obtained Non-Technical Objection/technical concurrence from manufacturer instead of approved data for flight extension for following purposes:
a)	Ferry flight aircraft back to maintenance base to carry out the maintenance in order to recover the airworthiness of the aircraft;
b)	Ferry flight to point of parking or storage;
c)	Delivery, re-delivery of aircraft;
d)	To evacuate the aircraft out of the dangerous zone due to natural disaster,enemy catastrophe, war or instability of the political and security situation.
The Ferry Flight Permit shall be valid only once and is not valid for any flight ofcommercial purpose.
2.26.8	Procedure
Ferry flight dossier shall submit to CAAV as soon as practicable but not later than 03 days before the intended day to conduct ferry flight.
Dossier for the ferry flight permit shall include the following documents:
a)	Ferry Flight Permit form (form CAAV/FSSD-AIR027)
b)	Detailed information on the defect of the aircraft or limitation including the reasons why the defect cannot be carried out at the place of defect occurrence;
c)	Additional required maintenance action if any to ensure the safe ferry flight including the time limit and specific conditions for such maintenance action;
d)	The recommendations of the aircraft manufacturer (NTO, technical concurrence, etc.) for flight extension and proposal of VJC in order to ensure the safe ferry flight.
The Technical Services Section is responsible for preparation of above dossier and provide to TQA Department for evaluation and further approval.
TQA engineer will evaluate and complete Ferry Flight Permit and submit to SQA Director/TQA Manager for approval before submission to CAAV.
Upon approval by the CAAV, Ferry Flight Permit shall be provided to OMC, MOC to conduct the ferry flight.
2.26.9	Condition of Ferry Flight Permit
Aircraft flying with Ferry Flight Permit issued by CAAV shall be subject to the following conditions:
a)	A copy of Ferry Flight Permit shall be carried out on board the aircraft when operating under ferry flight permit.
b)	The registration number of the aircraft issued by the CAAV must be displayed onthe aircraft in conformity with the regulations of the CAAV;
c)	Not allowed to transport passengers and cargo for commercial purpose;
d)	No person shall be carried on the aircraft unless that person is essential for the purpose of the flight and has been advised of the contents of the permit and airworthiness status of aircraft;
e)	The aircraft shall be operated only by flight crew who are aware of the purpose of the flight and any limitation imposed, and who hold appropriate license issued or validated by CAAV;
f)	All flights shall be conducted so as to avoid areas where flights might create hazardous exposures to person or property;
g)	All flights shall be conducted within the performance operating limitation prescribed in the Aircraft Flight Manual and any additional limitations prescribed for the particular flight;
h)	All flights must be carried out within the validity of the flight permit;
i)	If the flight involves operation over States other Vietnam, VJC shall obtain necessary overfly authorization from the respective authorities of each of those States prior to undertaking the flight.
2.26.10	Post ferry flight
Upon completion of ferry flight, SQA Director/TQA Manager shall report to CAAV and authority who had issued the ferry flight permit. The report should be sent via email and included following information:
a)	Any abnormally encountered during flight;
b)	Action taken at base to recover the airworthiness of the aircraft;
c)	Any other information regarding the flight as deemed necessary.
Ferry flight permit and relevant document, records shall be kept by TQAD within 03 years.

2.27.1	Purpose
This process describes the requirements and procedures to accept and approve VJC’s instructor for VJC’s maintenance procedure training including MME, LMM, PBN-RNP, RII, RVSM, AUTOLAND CAT II/III, De / Anti icing, PIC Transit Check ...procedures.
2.27.2	Scope of Application
This procedure is applicable for granting authorization and controlling the instructor – who will conduct VietJet Maintenance Procedures.
2.27.3	Reference
Appendix 1 VAR 12.227(18)(x).
MNT 1.10.5, 4.4.1, 4.4.2, 4.5.1
2.27.4	Responsibility
TQA Section, Technical Training Section, Engineering Department, VJC AMO and Contracted AMO have responsibilities to comply with this procedure.
2.27.5	Policy
2.27.5.1	Definitions
VJC’s Instructor: VJC employee and assigned by Engineering Department and authorized/accepted by TQA Section as a Maintenance Procedures Instructor.
VJC’s In-house Instructor: CRS B1/B2 or equivalent or instructor assigned by contracted AMO and accepted by TQA Section as a Maintenance Procedures Instructor.
2.27.5.2	 Requirements for the Instructor
a)	VJC’s Instructor:
	Being VietJet staff.
	Experience in aviation engineering, aircraft maintenance within an aviation organization at least 3 years.
	Being able to read, write, and understand the English language.
	Being trained in Vietnam Aviation Regulation (VAR).
	Being trained in Train the Trainer or Instructor Skill or Pedagogic Training course.
	Being trained in Human Factor
	Being trained in Safety Management Systems course.
	Being successfully trained in respective course or having in-depth knowledge of respective subject (MME, LMM, PBN, RVSM, AUTOLAND CAT II/III, RII, DAP, PIC Transit Check…and the other Special Operations).
	Being able to build/update training curriculum and training material of respective subject (PBN, RVSM, AUTOLAND CAT II/III, RII, DAP, PIC Transit Check…and the other Special Operations).
b)	Contracted AMO In-house Instructor:
	Qualified staff holding the B1/ B2 license or equivalent or assigned by Contracted AMO as in house-instructor.
	Being trained/updated about VJC Maintenance Regulations and
	Procedures (MME, LMM, PBN, RVSM, AUTOLAND CAT II/III, RII, DAP…).
2.27.6	Procedure
2.27.6.1	Authorization for VJC’s Instructor
	The candidates will submit the application package including Application for Instructor Approval (Form ETF009) and relevant certificates or evidence to Tech Training Manager
	Upon successful verification, Technical Training Manager forward to these application packages to TQA Manager for assessment and approval.
	Authorization Period is valid for 24 months.
2.27.6.2	Authorization for in-house instructor
	Contracted AMO shall provide instructor documents including CV, Training Records, relevant certificates to Tech Training Manager.
	Upon successful verification, Technical Training Manager forward instructor documents to TQA Manager for approval.
	TQA Manager shall issue approval letter to Contracted AMO and Technical Training Manager if satisfactory.
	Authorization Period is valid for 24 months.
2.27.6.3	Revocation of Authorization for VJC Instructor and In-house Instructor
The revocation or suspension of instructor authorization shall be decided by TQA Manager in the following cases:
a)	The instructor fails to maintain required competency or instructional performance.
b)	Any violation of training procedures, safety regulations, or internal company rules.
c)	Failure to maintain required training records or recurrent qualification as specified.
d)	A formal recommendation is raised by relevant departments following review/evaluation.
When revocation or suspension is decided, the responsible manager shall issue an official written notification indicating the reason and effective period, and distribute it to concerned departments (Training, TQA, and relevant departments).
During the period of revocation or suspension, the instructor is not permitted to conduct any instructional, assessment, or OJT activities under the revoked/suspended authorization.

2.28.1	Purpose
This procedure describes A/C monitoring and maintenance procedure to meet the EDTO requirements prescribed in VAR and other related requirements approved by CAAV.
2.28.2	Scope
This procedure is applied for A330 fleet of VJC that is currently in EDTO operation
2.28.3	Reference
VAR Part 12.033, VAR Part 12.037
EASA Decision No.2003/12/RM and AMC 20-6. EDTO Manual
CAAV AC-10-005
ISM MNT 2.8.2
2.28.4	Responsibility
All the departments of VJC are responsible for complying with the policies, requirements and procedures related to EDTO.
2.28.5	Definition
EDTO is the operation of twin-engine A/C where the flight time at one engine inoperative cruise speed under standard conditions in still air, from a point on the route to and adequate alternate aerodrome, is greater than 120 minutes. EDTO is applied for routes above land and sea.
2.28.6	Procedure
For details refer to VJC’s EDTO Manual, approved by CAAV. The Manuals include the following maintenance procedures:
a)	EDTO Configuration Control
b)	Minimum Equipment List (MEL)
c)	EDTO Significant Systems
d)	EDTO Reliability Program
e)	Propulsion System Monitoring Program
f)	APU In-Flight Start Program
g)	Oil Consumption Monitoring Program
h)	Engine Condition Monitoring Program
i)	Verification Program
j)	Dual Maintenance On Similar Multi-System
k)	Centralized Maintenance Control
l)	EDTO Qualified Personnel
m)	Sub-Contract Maintenance
n)	EDTO Supplement Maintenance Program
o)	EDTO Training
p)	Communication Focal Point
q)	EDTO Pre-Departure Service Check

Component robbery can only be performed as a last resort when the required part is unavailable.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.29.2	Scope</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">This procedure is applied for VJC aircraft, all VJC AMO personnel, contracted AMO personnel, and other relevant departments involved in maintenance operations.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.29.3	Reference</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">VAR Part 05</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">CAAV AC-04-009</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.29.4	Responsibility</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Maintenance Operations Center (MOC) is in charge of initiating and authorizing this procedure. The MOC's responsibilities include evaluating the defect and aircraft status, proposing solutions (including verifying parts compatibility and airworthiness), authorizing to carry out the robbery (cannibalization) or swapping, issuing work orders, and coordinating with other departments like Technical Services, Planning.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Planning / Technical Services section: Provides technical support and guidance, including related AMP tasks, verification of part compatibility, airworthiness status confirmation, and review of applicable ADs/SBs/modifications. If MOC requests, the TSE/Planning team will provide additional support and clarification on the airworthiness condition and modification status of cannibalized components. If necessary, the Design Approval Holder (DAH) will be consulted to clarify technical details or secure required approvals.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Certifying Staff: Performs the physical removal, installation, inspection, and certification of parts, ensuring compliance with approved data.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Store/Logistics: Manages the storage, handling, and transportation of robbed/swapped parts according to approved procedures.</p><p style="margin-top: 12px; margin-bottom: 4px;"><strong>2.29.5	Procedure</strong></p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">a)	Definitions</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Component Robbery (Cannibalization): The removal of a serviceable component from one aircraft (donor) to install it on another aircraft (receiver) with an unserviceable component.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">LRU Swapping: is a troubleshooting and maintenance procedure involving the exchange of identical LRUs to isolate faults, facilitate aircraft dispatch under certain conditions, and gather data for analysis</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">Form Certification Certificate (or equivalent): this certificate form is issued according to AMO’s MOE/MOPM</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">b)	Authorization and Control</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	MOC has the authority to approve robbery/swapping requests, and the decision is made in consultation with other departments, including Technical Services and Planning.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	A formal request process is essential, with a Risk Assessment of Part Robbery (cannibalization) /Swapping outlining the reason for the action, the parts involved, and the donor and receiver aircraft.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Each request is reviewed for part compatibility, airworthiness, impact on donor aircraft, alternative solutions, and regulatory compliance.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">4)	All requests must be submitted via the designated form or email.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">5)	All requests are authorized by the Engineering Director/ Head of MOC or his/her delegated person (verbal or email).</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">c)	General Requirements</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	Strictly adhere to policy at MME 1.6.7 for Robbery (Cannibalization) of Component or Swapping.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	Certifying staff is responsible for the physical removal, installation, and certification of parts, following the procedures outlined in the AMM. Detailed documentation is crucial for all actions, including:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	Work orders</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	Aircraft technical log entries</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">	Form certification certificates (if applicable)</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">3)	Robbery (Cannibalization) and Swapping is only allowed in exceptional cases when a needed part is not available and is approved by the MOC. Common situations include:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">i.	AOG (Aircraft on Ground) situations that need to be fixed immediately.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">ii.	Troubleshooting when there is no other way to find the root cause of a technical problem.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">4)	Before removing a component in storage for robbery (cannibalization), its serviceability and configuration must be completely verified. This includes checking AMOS records, reviewing maintenance history, and performing a visual inspection. The component's status must be verified both on the aircraft and in AMOS to confirm its serviceability before proceeding.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">5)	Form Certification Certificate (or equivalent) would be issued following section 2.30 for details procedure of component certification.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">6)	VJC is responsible for providing VJC AMO/ contracted AMOs with approved documentation that enables them to validate the airworthiness of a part and its certification for installation. This documentation can include the original CAAV Form 1 or equivalent (such as FAA, EASA, TCCA, CAA UK, and ANAC…), along with other documents like MME, IPC, AD, SB, Work Order, and Repair Order.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">7)	If the donor/receiver aircraft is an EDTO-approved aircraft, VJC ensures that the policy addresses specific requirements for robbery (cannibalization)/swapping on EDTO aircraft according to EDTO manual (Section 5.10). For example, verify that the part meets EDTO standards and apply dual maintenance policy where necessary.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">8)	In cases where the donor aircraft is parked or in storage, VJC must confirm that the requirements for cannibalized components specified in VJC Parking and Storage Procedure have been fulfilled. Additionally, VJC must ensure that all required parking or storage maintenance tasks have been completed.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">d)	Component Robbery (cannibalization)</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">1)	MOC initially evaluates component robbery requests, detailing the required part, reason, and submits a risk assessment form (MOC 009) for approval.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">2)	MOC, in consultation with Technical Services and Planning, completes Form MOC 009. Engineering department (Technical Services, Planning, MOC) shall assess component serviceability and compatibility with the receiver aircraft, including:</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">i.	Technical Services shall review the related AD/SB.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">ii.	Planning shall review the related AMP tasks.</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">iii.	MOC shall review the related Acceptance Defferal Defects (ADDs)</p><p style="margin-bottom: 6px;">iv. 2.29.1	Purpose
This procedure establishes a controlled and compliant process for Robbery/ Cannibalization (removing a serviceable part from a donor aircraft for use on another aircraft) and Swapping (swapping parts for troubleshooting or dispatch purpose).
This procedure, developed in accordance with CAAV requirements, aims to address AOG situations or essential maintenance while maintaining the continued airworthiness of all affected aircraft and ensuring traceability of parts. Component robbery can only be performed as a last resort when the required part is unavailable.
2.29.2	Scope
This procedure is applied for VJC aircraft, all VJC AMO personnel, contracted AMO personnel, and other relevant departments involved in maintenance operations.
2.29.3	Reference
VAR Part 05
CAAV AC-04-009
2.29.4	Responsibility
Maintenance Operations Center (MOC) is in charge of initiating and authorizing this procedure. The MOC's responsibilities include evaluating the defect and aircraft status, proposing solutions (including verifying parts compatibility and airworthiness), authorizing to carry out the robbery (cannibalization) or swapping, issuing work orders, and coordinating with other departments like Technical Services, Planning.
Planning / Technical Services section: Provides technical support and guidance, including related AMP tasks, verification of part compatibility, airworthiness status confirmation, and review of applicable ADs/SBs/modifications. If MOC requests, the TSE/Planning team will provide additional support and clarification on the airworthiness condition and modification status of cannibalized components. If necessary, the Design Approval Holder (DAH) will be consulted to clarify technical details or secure required approvals.
Certifying Staff: Performs the physical removal, installation, inspection, and certification of parts, ensuring compliance with approved data.
Store/Logistics: Manages the storage, handling, and transportation of robbed/swapped parts according to approved procedures.
2.29.5	Procedure
a)	Definitions
Component Robbery (Cannibalization): The removal of a serviceable component from one aircraft (donor) to install it on another aircraft (receiver) with an unserviceable component.
LRU Swapping: is a troubleshooting and maintenance procedure involving the exchange of identical LRUs to isolate faults, facilitate aircraft dispatch under certain conditions, and gather data for analysis
Form Certification Certificate (or equivalent): this certificate form is issued according to AMO’s MOE/MOPM
b)	Authorization and Control
1)	MOC has the authority to approve robbery/swapping requests, and the decision is made in consultation with other departments, including Technical Services and Planning.
2)	A formal request process is essential, with a Risk Assessment of Part Robbery (cannibalization) /Swapping outlining the reason for the action, the parts involved, and the donor and receiver aircraft.
3)	Each request is reviewed for part compatibility, airworthiness, impact on donor aircraft, alternative solutions, and regulatory compliance.
4)	All requests must be submitted via the designated form or email.
5)	All requests are authorized by the Engineering Director/ Head of MOC or his/her delegated person (verbal or email).
c)	General Requirements
1)	Strictly adhere to policy at MME 1.6.7 for Robbery (Cannibalization) of Component or Swapping.
2)	Certifying staff is responsible for the physical removal, installation, and certification of parts, following the procedures outlined in the AMM. Detailed documentation is crucial for all actions, including:
	Work orders
	Aircraft technical log entries
	Form certification certificates (if applicable)
3)	Robbery (Cannibalization) and Swapping is only allowed in exceptional cases when a needed part is not available and is approved by the MOC. Common situations include:
i.	AOG (Aircraft on Ground) situations that need to be fixed immediately.
ii.	Troubleshooting when there is no other way to find the root cause of a technical problem.
4)	Before removing a component in storage for robbery (cannibalization), its serviceability and configuration must be completely verified. This includes checking AMOS records, reviewing maintenance history, and performing a visual inspection. The component's status must be verified both on the aircraft and in AMOS to confirm its serviceability before proceeding.
5)	Form Certification Certificate (or equivalent) would be issued following section 2.30 for details procedure of component certification.
6)	VJC is responsible for providing VJC AMO/ contracted AMOs with approved documentation that enables them to validate the airworthiness of a part and its certification for installation. This documentation can include the original CAAV Form 1 or equivalent (such as FAA, EASA, TCCA, CAA UK, and ANAC…), along with other documents like MME, IPC, AD, SB, Work Order, and Repair Order.
7)	If the donor/receiver aircraft is an EDTO-approved aircraft, VJC ensures that the policy addresses specific requirements for robbery (cannibalization)/swapping on EDTO aircraft according to EDTO manual (Section 5.10). For example, verify that the part meets EDTO standards and apply dual maintenance policy where necessary.
8)	In cases where the donor aircraft is parked or in storage, VJC must confirm that the requirements for cannibalized components specified in VJC Parking and Storage Procedure have been fulfilled. Additionally, VJC must ensure that all required parking or storage maintenance tasks have been completed.
d)	Component Robbery (cannibalization)
1)	MOC initially evaluates component robbery requests, detailing the required part, reason, and submits a risk assessment form (MOC 009) for approval.
2)	MOC, in consultation with Technical Services and Planning, completes Form MOC 009. Engineering department (Technical Services, Planning, MOC) shall assess component serviceability and compatibility with the receiver aircraft, including:
i.	Technical Services shall review the related AD/SB.
ii.	Planning shall review the related AMP tasks.
iii.	MOC shall review the related Acceptance Defferal Defects (ADDs)
iv.	Technical Services/ Planning shall verify component condition and history (especially for HT/LLP parts).
v.	MOC evaluates the potential impact on the receiver aircraft's operational status (e.g., EDTO), including operational limitations and proposing mitigation actions in consultation with Technical Services.
vi.	MOC evaluates the potential impact on the donor aircraft, including impact on the aircraft (especially if in storage), proposing mitigation actions in consultation with Technical Services, and considering component reinstallation timelines and replacement part availability.
vii.	In case of discrepancies or ambiguities, Technical Services shall escalate to the DAH for further verification.
3)	Upon approval, MOC issues a work order for robbery/ cannibalization and attaches a completed risk assessment form.
4)	The Approved Maintenance Organization (AMO) can assess the risk assessments if necessary.
5)	Certifying staff must review aircraft records and maintenance history for any unusual events (especially in accidents, incidents, heavy landings, lightning strikes, etc.) that could affect the part's serviceability.
6)	Certifying staff shall perform checks component status and confirm its serviceability before removing a component from a donor aircraft.
7)	Certifying staff on the donor aircraft will perform the component removal in accordance with the approved maintenance technical data of the aircraft Type Certificate (TC) holder or the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).
8)	For component removal from stored aircraft:
i.	Certifying staff verifies component serviceability through functional/operational tests and inspections before removal, recording findings in the Aircraft Technical Log.
ii.	After removal, the component is stored and preserved following AMO's MOE/ MOPM.
9)	Certifying staff records into the Aircraft Technical Log (including date, aircraft registration, part number, serial number, reason for removal, condition, test/inspection results, LLP details, and AD compliance status), and protect the removed part . Component certification shall also be issued according to MME 2.30 ‘Certifying component’. However, it’s not necessary to issue certification certificate if the cannibalized aircraft component is directly installed on the other aircraft at same location and by same certifying staff.
e)	Part Swapping
1)	A formal request can be initiated either verbally or via email by maintenance personnel or MOC personnel. The request must include: aircraft registration, LRU part number and description, reason for the swap (troubleshooting, dispatch, etc.) and verification plan (if applicable).
2)	MOC, consult with Technical Services section if required, reviews the reviews the swap request. MOC approves or rejects the request.
3)	Upon approval, MOC shall issue WO to request certifying staff to swap the LRU. However, WO issuance is not required when a defect is newly raised and a swap is needed for dispatch. All maintenance actions are recorded into the Aircraft Technical Log, referencing the work order, AMM procedures, and relevant details (P/N, S/N, positions)
4)	Specific requirements for component verification:
i.	Swapping is only permitted if the AMM, IPC, MEL, or other approved data do not list the LRUs as non-allowable for swapping.
ii.	Troubleshooting:
	When a reported fault cannot be confirmed on the ground, identical LRUs can be swapped on the same aircraft for troubleshooting. MOC must follow up on the aircraft's status for further assessment
	If the root cause of a fault remains unclear, LRUs can be swapped on the same aircraft for monitoring with an existing ADD in place. An NTC is raised to annotate the swap. MOC follows up and may request an engineer onboard if needed.
	Identical LRUs can be swapped between aircraft at the same station for ground troubleshooting. If the faulty LRU is identified or not, both LRUs must be returned to their original positions. During ground troubleshooting, the "GRN ON" entry in the Aircraft Technical Log shall be the aircraft registration number of the aircraft from which the LRU was originally removed.
iii.	Dispatch purpose
If a suspected faulty LRU is a NO-GO item per the MEL in its original position, or less penalizing in another position, it can be swapped with an identical LRU on the same aircraft under the following conditions:
	The LRU is confirmed faulty by the TSM.
	The TSM does not prohibit swapping.
	Swapping is not used to extend dispatch under MEL conditions.
	MEL procedures and limitations are applied to the LRU in its new position.
	Corrective maintenance is carried out as soon as possible, within the MEL time limit.
	Both LRUs have dedicated circuit breakers.
	The faulty LRU is de-energized in its new position.
	A BITE test is performed on the LRU installed in the original position
iv.	All swapping actions must be recorded in the Aircraft Technical Log, including:
	Reason for the swap.
	Work order reference.
	AMM and TSM references.
	LRU details (P/N, S/N).
	Original and new positions of the swapped LRUs (LH, RH, FIN…).
	Aircraft registration numbers (if swapped between aircraft).","translatedText":"","isVerbatim":true},"2.30":{"id":"2.30","code":"2.30","title":"2.30 CERTIFYING COMPONENT","chapter":"Section 2.30 - CERTIFYING COMPONENT","partTitle":"PART 2","partId":"doc_1787632969907_p_2","htmlContent":"<h3 style="font-weight: bold; 2.30.1	Purpose
To ensure that all used components removed from VJC aircraft are re-certified as serviceable, adhering to all applicable safety and airworthiness regulations, approved maintenance data, and internal procedures, contributing to the overall safety of aircraft operations.
2.30.2	Scope
This procedure applies to all serviceable components removed from VJC aircraft, encompassing situations like:
	Troubleshooting or identification of technical issues.
	Robbery (Cannibalization) in AOG (Aircraft On Ground) circumstances or when troubleshooting.
	Removal from aircraft withdrawn from service.
Scheduled maintenance tasks as directed by Engineering Orders (EOs), Work Orders (WOs), or other approved maintenance instructions.
2.30.3	Reference
VJC MME 1.6.4, MME 2.29
CAAV VAR 4.045, 4.083, 4.095, 4.103
CAAV VAR 5.115, 5.150
CAAV AC 04-009
2.30.4	Responsibility
a)	MOC requests the removal of components for robbery/ cannibalization, provide information including: associated work orders, airworthiness status (such as AMP, HT/LLP, AD/SB, etc.), risk assessment of cannibalized parts/ systems/ components.
b)	Engineering Department has responsible for providing VJC AMO/ contracted AMOs with approved maintenance data for preservation/ storage condition if necessary.
c)	VJC AMO/ Contracted AMOs are obligated to conduct incoming inspections on all VJC components to verify compliance with established documentation standards and assess part condition. These AMOs must strictly adhere to MME 1.6.4.5 for component handling, preservation (storage), maintenance, and certification.
d)	Certifying staff assumes ultimate responsibility for confirming the airworthiness of the component meet all applicable requirements before being certified component.
2.30.5	Policy
a)	All certification activities must comply with CAAV regulations.
b)	The certified component meets all safety and airworthiness standards.
c)	MOC approval is required for all component robbery actions. VJC Engineering department will verify component airworthiness, compatibility, and regulatory implications.
d)	A certified component traceability system must be in place, utilizing AMOS, unique identification labels, and detailed documentation to track component movements and maintain accurate configuration control.
e)	Serviceable components are removed and maintained in storage:
1)	Maintained storage of component according to AMO’s MOE/MOPM.
2)	In case of undefined environmental storage conditions for component removed, Engineering Department is responsible for providing VJC AMO/ contracted AMOs with approved maintenance data that enables AMOs to maintain the airworthiness condition of a part in storage.
2.30.6	Procedure
a)	MOC shall review and provide information of component identification, including:
1)	MOC shall review the component's last flight operational history and any associated defect reports.
2)	MOC shall provide documentation, including the component's description, part number, serial number, and airworthiness status (e.g., AMP, HT/LLP, AD/SB, etc.) via associated work orders and risk assessment of cannibalized parts/systems/components.
b)	Certifying staff perform the assessment of serviceability, including:
1)	Confirm normal operation during the last flight with no evidence of defects. If any defects occurred, ensure proper troubleshooting, repair, and verification according to approved data.
2)	Verify compliance with all applicable ADs and SBs, HT/LLP and AMP requirements based on information provided by MOC.
3)	Check the component's history based on information provided by MOC.
4)	Inspect to ensure no physical damage, corrosion, leak or any other unserviceable condition. In case of defect on component removed, it shall be assessed according to approved data and informed to MOC. Accepted Deferral Defects (ADDs) information shall be recorded in Certification Certificate form.
5)	For component removal from stored aircraft, certifying staff must verify component serviceability through functional/operational tests and inspections according to associated work orders before removal.
c)	Upon removal, certifying staff shall issue a Certification Certificate:
1)	Complete the AMO’s certification form. These forms include:
a. Approved organization name and address
b. Item description, part number, quantity, and serial number
c. Work order number
d. Donor aircraft registration (if applicable)
e. State "Airworthiness Status/ Work”.
f. Remarks (specifying details such as the aircraft the part was removed from, the work order it was certified under this procedure, related ADDs, component's history, applicable ADs/SBs, HT/LLP, AMP requirements and storage & testing instructions)
2)	Certifying staff shall record all work, inspections, and certifications in the aircraft technical log and associated work orders.

2.31.1	Objective
This maintenance procedure ensures the effective maintenance of Controller-Pilot Data-Link Communication (CPDLC) and Automatic Dependent Surveillance – Contract (ADS-C) systems, enabling seamless communication and surveillance between aircraft flight crews and Air Traffic Services (ATS) units.
2.31.2	Scope
This maintenance procedure ensures the effective maintenance of Controller-Pilot Data-Link Communication (CPDLC) and Automatic Dependent Surveillance – Contract (ADS-C) systems, enabling seamless communication and surveillance between aircraft flight crews and Air Traffic Services (ATS) units.
2.31.3	References
	ICAO Doc 10037 (Global Operational Data Link (GOLD) Manual)
	VAR Part 6
	CAAV AC 10-013
	A330 AFM
	IOSA MNT 2.9.2
	VJC Datalink Manual
2.31.4	Responsibilities
a)	The Engineering Director is responsible for ensuring compliance with the CPDLC and ADS-C configuration and maintenance program.
b)	The Training Department is responsible for developing CPDLC/ADS-C maintenance training programs, and providing the CPDLC/ADS-C maintenance training to VJC technical staff, VJC AMO (Aircraft Maintenance Organization), and contracted AMO.
c)	The Technical Quality Assurance (TQA) Department is responsible for reviewing and validating CPDLC and ADS-C maintenance records and procedures, and CPDLC/ADS-C instructor authorization
d)	The contracted AMO is responsible for implementing all CPDLC/ADS-C maintenance in accordance with approved procedures.
2.31.5	System Description
a)	The FANS-1/A+ is dedicated to operation over oceanic, and remote areas. This FANS-1/A+ supports the following data-link services over the ACARS network:
1)	Automatic Dependent Surveillance on Contract (ADS-C);
2)	Air Traffic Service (ATS) Facilities Notification (AFN);
3)	Controller Pilot Data Link Communication (CPDLC).
b)	ADS-C allows ATS units to automatically receive position and intent reports from the aircraft based on predefined contracts.
c)	CPDLC is a means of communication between air traffic controller and pilot, using data-link for ATC communications.
d)	VHF (VDL mode 2) and SATCOM are used for the CPDLC data-link communication.
e)	Air Traffic Service Unit (ATSU) with dedicated software is equipped to host data-link communication for CPDLC and ADS-C application.
f)	CPDLC and ADS-C involve the exchange of per-formatted or free text messages. All ATC messages, either coming from the ATC center (uplink) or to be sent to the ATC center (downlink), transit through the Data-link Control and Display Unit (DCDU).
g)	Crew members are warned of any new ATC messages reception by two ATC MSG push-buttons located on the glare-shield, and use dedicated display units (DCDU) to handle data-link messages sending and reception.
h)	According to the VJC A330 AFM, the aircraft’s CPDLC and ADS-C applications have been demonstrated to comply with the aircraft-allocated performance requirements as follows:

a)	All VJC A330 aircraft have the certified FANS-1/A+ configuration that includes AFN, CPDLC, and ADS-C capability.
b)	The required equipment installed on VJC’s A330 fleet for the CPDLC/ADS-C capability is as follows (Ref. AC 10-013 Para. 4.2.4, MMEL, and MEL):
